title: Pilot escalation roleplay scripts for field teams (draft)
body:
Purpose: quick, repeatable roleplay scripts for SEs/AE/CS when a paid pilot hits a live operational or quality escalation. Focus is on de-escalation, preserving trust, collecting triage data, and enabling an immediate customer-facing action plan (24–72h window).

Scope and audience: field sellers, customer engineers, solutions engineers, CSMs running pilots with Dedicated or Private deployments. Not a full postmortem playbook — this is the immediate first 4 hours and up to 72 hours.

How to use this doc: skim the scenario headings, choose the script that matches the customer symptom, run a 10–15 minute roleplay with your SE/AE/CS partner before calling the customer. Keep one person on notes/next steps. After call, file a brief incident note in JIRA and attach the call recording/transcript.

Quick checklist before dialing (2–5 minutes):
- Confirm: pilot name, contact roles on call, expected SLOs for the pilot (latency, throughput, accuracy).
- Pre-collect: model+version, endpoint URL, region, request id(s) if available.
- Prep fallback: which model variant to suggest (smaller/larger/quantized), suggested temporary rate-limit or sampling setting, and a short remediation timeline (e.g., "we can revert to cached responses in 2 hours").
- Decide the lead: AE handles contract/po/expectations; SE owns technical triage; CSM owns comms and next steps.

Scenario A — "High latency spikes in production queries" (common)
Symptoms: intermittent 2–10x latency spikes, usually tied to larger context lengths or EMR-style batch backpressure. Customers report timeouts or user-visible slowdowns.
Script (roles: AE opens, SE triages, CSM notes):
- AE (0:00–0:30): "Thanks for making time. We heard you saw slow responses beginning yesterday afternoon. We want to keep this short and get clear next steps — first, can you confirm the top example request IDs or the user flow you saw the slow path on?"
- Customer provides IDs or flow.
- SE (0:30–2:00): "Thank you — quick diagnostics questions: 1) are these single long prompts or a stream of short prompts? 2) did you recently change max_tokens/streaming settings or add function/tool calls? 3) can we ask for a sample payload (anonymized) to run locally?"
- If customer gives payload: SE reproduces ideally within 15–30 minutes on a staging environment and reports: "I can reproduce a 3x spike when context > 3k tokens (we see KV cache churn). Our immediate mitigation is to enable prefix caching and drop the default batch size from 64 to 16 for this route; this will lower spikes at the expense of marginal throughput. We can push the change within 2 hours with no schema changes."
- AE (2:00–2:30): "We will do that change and monitor. If it’s acceptable, we’ll keep you updated with a health check in 4 hours and a short RCA in 48–72 hours."
- CSM (close): "Next steps summarized: change X by 2h, monitor, healthcheck at 4h, RCA by EOD+2. Point of contact: SE Marco Li (x) and AE Asha Patel (x)."

Notes / escalation triggers: if latency persists after two config iterations -> escalate to infra SRE (tag: SRE-PILOT). If we see error rate > 1% or CPU/GPU saturations -> escalate to serving-runtime oncall.

Scenario B — "Model hallucination/regression halfway through pilot"
Symptoms: Previously acceptable answer quality drops: confident-but-incorrect facts, hallucinated references, or high variance between runs. Customer is citing production user complaints and wants to pause.
Script (roles: SE lead, AE frames business impact, Research/Applied ML notified):
- AE (0:00–0:30): "We understand output quality matters a lot — thank you for surfacing the examples. Our priority is to (a) stop further user impact, (b) capture representative prompts, and (c) produce a short plan to revert or tune. Can we confirm whether the examples are from the same model version or multiple versions?"
- SE (0:30–3:00): "Immediate ask: please share 3–10 anonymized prompt-response pairs. We will: 1) run them through the model evaluation harness, 2) check for recent model swaps/rollouts, and 3) compare tokenization or pre-processing changes. If needed, we can temporarily pin to the prior model version within 1 hour and roll back traffic."
- Research/Applied ML (if engaged): quick triage to determine whether the issue is model-level (new weights) vs prompt-stage. If model-level, propose: roll back to verified commit + run regression bench; if prompt-stage, propose: canonicalize pre-processing or add a guardrail filter.
- AE (close): "We will keep the pilot running in a read-only or redirected mode until the RCA; we propose 24–48 hours for a mitigation plan and we will log a postmortem in the pilot Jira."

Customer communications guidance (tone):
- Always lead with: "We understand the customer impact and we’re on it."
- Avoid technical blame or speculation in first message (e.g., no "it’s the model" or "it’s your code").
- Use simple timelines and named owners.
- Offer short-term mitigations (e.g., pin to previous model, reduce sampling temp, remove uncertain tool-calls) and commit to a timeboxed RCA.

Scenario C — "Security or data residency questions during private deployment"
Symptoms: Legal/security notices, SOC2/ISO questions, or a surprise audit request. Customer requests evidence or for service to be paused pending review.
Script (roles: AE sets expectations, Security lead/PS engaged):
- AE (0:00–1:00): "Thanks — we treat any security/residency concern as high priority. We’ll pause the production route if you prefer and will fetch the artifact list. To triage quickly: can you confirm the scope of data in question (PII, customer data, logs) and any regulatory references?"
- Security/PS (1:00–ongoing): pull KMS/HSM logs, access audit trails, and validate network boundaries. Provide a preliminary evidence report within 24 hours.
- AE (close): Provide suggested customer-facing wording: "We will pause the route and provide a preliminary evidence package within 24 hours and a full compliance package within 5 business days. Named contacts: Security — Sofia Nguyen; AE — Asha Patel."

Roleplay script example (short):
- SE (mock customer): "We just saw an example of a customer name in a generated reply and we’re worried about leakage."
- AE (response): "I’m really sorry you saw that — I know this is alarming. We will pause the route to prevent further exposure and will begin a targeted search for the source. Can you share any IDs or timestamps? While we investigate, we will keep the pilot paused and update you in 24 hours with initial findings."

Escalation matrix (quick view):
- Immediate (0–4h): Field SE/AE/CSM triage.
- Near-term (4–24h): Platform SRE, Serving-runtime oncall, Research if quality issue.
- Formal (24–72h): Security/legal, Dedicated engineering leads, account exec for contractual impacts.

Post-call artifacts to produce (always):
- Short incident summary (1–2 paragraphs) in Jira with tags and customer contact.
- Named owners + 24/48/72h milestones.
- Actionable temporary mitigations (config changes, pinned model id, traffic throttling).
- Call recording + anonymized payloads attached for debug.

Roleplay variations and prompts (for practicing):
- Angry customer persona: short, to-the-point, high cost impact. Practice empathy and rapid mitigation offers.
- Curious engineer persona: wants logs, traces, and deeper technical explanation. Be ready to hand-off to SE or SRE.
- Procurement/legal persona: focused on contract and liability language — don’t overpromise; instead promise an evidence package.

Notes to trainers: run 15–20 minute drills with a live marker to time the AE/SE handoffs. Keep scripts loose — the important parts are named owners, short mitigation commitments, and an artifact (Jira entry) created before ending the call.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Create a short template for the Jira incident that includes the minimal fields we need (customer impact, pilot id, model id, example requests, immediate mitigation, 24h owner). Jira ticket JIRA-PILOT-58 is a placeholder for suggested template work.
- Decide whether we want a canned outbound email templates for each scenario (suggested: one for latency, one for hallucinations, one for security).
- Add quick checklist for on-call routing phone numbers and Slack channels (SRE, serving-runtime, research) — currently manual.

References and links for deeper drills:
- Pilot telemetry dashboard (internal): keep handy during roleplays.
- Oncall runbooks: SRE, Serving-runtime.
- Legal: standard contract clauses for pilot usage and liability.

Notes to self (informal):
- This doc should live near pilot templates not in central sales deck folder.
- We should run a cross-functional tabletop next quarter with SRE + Research + AE to validate timelines.
- Consider a short video of a sample roleplay for new SEs.

End of draft.
